## Zoom G3Xn "Princeton Warm" Patch Checklist

Guitar: Fender Telecaster MIJ, neck pickup, Master Volume ~9, Master Tone ~9
Amp: Fender Blues Jr III (real amp, miked — no Zoom amp/cab sim used)
Zoom: G3Xn, Firmware 2.20, Patch cell 106, Patch name "Princeton"
Goal: Warm, articulate Princeton Reverb-style clean tone with shimmer trem and spring reverb

---

## Signal Chain

Guitar → RackComp → RC Boost → Tremolo → FD Spring → Zoom output → Blues Jr input → mic

Note: guitar Volume/Tone currently near max (~9/~9) rather than rolled back. Brighter/more
aggressive than original plan — if tone feels too bright or aggressive once recorded, roll
Tone back to 6-7 as first adjustment.

---

## Block 1 — RackComp (DYNAMICS)

- [x] THRSH: 25
- [x] Ratio: 3
- [x] ATTCK: 5
- [x] VOL: 100 (unity/pass-through — not a boost like RC Boost's Volume)

## Block 2 — RC Boost (DRIVE)

- [x] Gain: 15
- [x] Bass: 50
- [x] Treble: 55
- [x] VOL: 65 (adjusted down from 100/max after A/B testing — 100 was a noticeable level jump, not a subtle push)

## Block 3 — Tremolo (MODULATION)

- [x] Wave: **TUBE**
- [x] Depth: 35
- [x] Rate: 30
- [x] VOL: 100

## Block 4 — FD Spring (REVERB) — sole reverb source (Option A)

- [x] Active: ON
- [x] Color: 1
- [x] Lo: 55
- [x] Hi: 45
- [x] Mix: 30

Decision: FD Spring is the sole *meaningful* reverb source. Blues Jr's physical Reverb
dial has no true zero (range is 1–12), so it stays at its physical minimum (1) — this
contributes a negligible touch of onboard spring underneath and is not treated as
problematic stacking.

---

## Block 5 — Rhythm (RHYTHM AND LOOPER) — practice aid, not part of the recorded tone

- [x] Active: ON (intentional — metronome for practice)
- Pattern: Metro4 4/4
- Volume: 4
- **Reminder: disable or mute before any actual take** — this is a metronome click, not a tone-shaping effect, and isn't meant to bleed into the final recording

---

## Amp Settings — Blues Jr III (dials 1–12, no true zero)

- [x] Volume: 4.5
- [x] Fat: OFF
- [x] Treble: 5.5
- [x] Bass: 4.5
- [x] Middle: 5.0
- [x] Master: 4.5
- [x] Reverb: 1 (physical minimum — FD Spring on the Zoom is the sole meaningful reverb source, see Block 4)

---

## Mic Setup — Blue Yeti (on stock desktop stand, floor placement)

- [ ] Mode: Cardioid
- [ ] Orientation: **logo side of mesh grille facing the amp** (this is the capsule's listening face — confirmed correct)
- [ ] Distance: 4–5 inches from grille
- [ ] Position: base shifted slightly to the **right** of the amp's centerline (creates true off-axis angle, since the stock stand doesn't swivel sideways)
- [ ] Tilt: forward, toward the amp — this aims the capsule up to cone height (compensating for the stand sitting lower than the speaker on the floor)
- [ ] Gain: set using the *loudest* tremolo peak, target -12 to -6 dB, no clipping

Notes:
- Forward tilt = vertical aim adjustment (reaches cone height), not the off-axis angle
- Sideways base offset = true off-axis angle (softens pick attack/harshness)
- Both adjustments are used together in this floor setup since the stand can't swivel independently

---

## Test Pass

- [ ] Turn OFF/mute Rhythm (metronome) block before recording an actual take
- [ ] Record 15–20 seconds of comping/chords
- [ ] RC Boost check: at Volume 65, should feel like a mild lift, not an obvious pedal jump. Adjust down further (55–60) if still too pushed.
- [ ] Reverb check: FD Spring is the sole meaningful reverb source (amp Reverb sits at its physical minimum of 1) — confirm the overall reverb amount feels right, not doubled
- [ ] Tremolo check: TUBE wave should feel smoother/rounder than a standard triangle wave trem
- [ ] Compression check: RackComp should be felt as sustain/evenness, not obvious pumping
- [ ] Guitar tone check: Volume/Tone near max (~9/~9) — if the result feels too bright/aggressive, roll Tone back to 6–7 first
- [ ] Overall: does the amp feel like it's "working" a little (natural compression) rather than stiff/clean?
- [ ] If still too clean/stiff: raise Master first, before touching EQ
